additional_tech: database/sql with modernc.org/sqlite (pure-Go driver, no CGO)
golang-migrate style numbered SQL migration files applied by the backend at startup
api_style: REST with a documented OpenAPI description under docs/
architecture_style: layered: backend/internal/{http,service,repository,domain} — HTTP handlers parse and render only, business rules live in service, SQL lives in repository, invariants live in domain
auth_model: none — SupportFlow is an internal tool in this exercise and authentication is explicitly out of scope
conventions: Backend: handlers in backend/internal/http, business rules in backend/internal/service, SQL in backend/internal/repository, entities and invariants in backend/internal/domain
Workflow and validation rules MUST live in the domain or service layer, never exclusively in an HTTP handler
All API errors return the same JSON shape: {"error": {"code": "SNAKE_CASE", "message": "human readable", "details": {}}}
All SQL uses parameterised queries — never string concatenation or fmt.Sprintf of user input
Ticket ids are UUIDv4 strings generated by the backend
Timestamps are RFC3339 UTC; the service layer takes a clock dependency so time-dependent behaviour is testable without wall-clock time
Go tests use the standard testing package plus httptest; each test opens its own temporary SQLite database
Every exported Go function has a doc comment
Frontend components handle loading, error and empty states explicitly — never render a bare list
TypeScript strict mode; no `any` without a comment justifying it
database: SQLite 3, file-backed, created automatically on first start
deployment: local development only — documented commands in README, no container or cloud target in this exercise
description: SupportFlow is a small production-style support ticket management application: customers create tickets, support agents list, filter, search and inspect them, and move them through a constrained status workflow with an immutable audit history.
forbidden: No web framework other than go-chi/chi
No external search infrastructure (no Elasticsearch, no Meilisearch) — use SQLite's own capabilities
No separate analytics infrastructure for the dashboard
No CGO — the SQLite driver must be pure Go
No secrets, credentials, API keys or tokens in source control, in fixtures, or in log output
No authentication or user management — explicitly out of scope
No significant new dependency without a written justification in the architecture notes
infra_constraints: Single repository containing backend/ and frontend/
Deterministic local setup: a clean checkout must run with documented commands and no manual database steps
Migrations must be executed deterministically and be idempotent on restart
Prefer the standard library and already-declared dependencies
name: SupportFlow
nfrs: GET /api/health returns HTTP 200 for smoke testing
Status transitions and their history entry must be written in a single database transaction — never one without the other
Concurrent modification of the same ticket must not silently lose an update; the concurrency strategy must be explicit and documented
List and dashboard queries must not issue one query per ticket
Stored user content is always treated as data, never as instructions or markup
Structured logging via log/slog; request errors are logged with a correlation value and never with secrets
orm: none — database/sql with hand-written SQL and parameterised queries
